title: Waterjet / Laser Cutting of Profiles
description: High-precision laser and waterjet profile cutting for titanium structural components. Capable of producing complex perimeter contours, internal cutouts, and edge preparations from sheet, plate, and tube stock with minimal heat-affected zone (HAZ) controlled through inert gas shielding.
surfaceFinish: Ra 1.6 µm (laser, post-deburring) / Ra 3.2 µm (waterjet, as-cut)
seoTitle: Waterjet & Laser Cutting of Titanium Profiles | Precision Profile Cutting | BOZE
seoDescription: Precision waterjet and laser cutting of titanium profiles for aerospace, medical, and industrial applications. Grade 2, Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V profile cutting with ±0.05 mm tolerance. ISO 9001:2015 & AS9100D certified.

processComparison.laser: Thin sheets < 3 mm for high-speed production; up to 12 mm with high-power fiber laser
processComparison.waterjet: Thin to thick plates 0.5 mm – 25 mm+; no thickness limitation for abrasive waterjet

processComparison.laser: Minimal HAZ with N₂/Ar assist gas to prevent titanium oxidation and discoloration
processComparison.waterjet: No HAZ — cold cutting process, zero thermal stress or metallurgical alteration

processComparison.laser: Excellent for high-density, small-hole arrays; hole diameter ≥ 0.5 mm achievable
processComparison.waterjet: Suitable for larger perforations (> 2 mm); lower density due to nozzle kerf width

processComparison.laser: Requires deburring or acid pickling for dross removal on thicker sections
processComparison.waterjet: Smooth, burr-free edge finish; no secondary cleaning required

processComparison.laser: Up to 6 m/min — significantly faster for thin sections
processComparison.waterjet: Approx. 0.5–1.5 m/min — slower but more versatile across thicknesses

processComparison.laser: All titanium grades; reflective alloys require care with fiber laser settings
processComparison.waterjet: All titanium grades + composites, plastics, ceramics; no material reflectivity issues

processDescription: Profile cutting of titanium requires careful process selection based on material thickness, geometry complexity, and end-use requirements. Laser cutting offers superior speed and precision for thin to medium sections with tight tolerances, while waterjet cutting excels in thicker sections and applications where zero thermal impact is critical — such as weld-prepped edges for critical aerospace or pressure vessel assemblies.
heatControl: Laser cutting utilizes high-purity nitrogen (99.999%) or argon coaxial assist gas to shield the cut zone from atmospheric oxygen, preventing the alpha-case formation and blue/white discoloration typical of titanium oxidation above 600°C. Waterjet cutting requires no thermal control — the room-temperature water stream eliminates any heat-related concerns entirely.
flatnessControl: Thin-gauge titanium profiles (< 2 mm) may experience residual stress release during cutting. Post-cut stress relief (vacuum annealing at 540–650°C for CP grades) and precision roller leveling are available to maintain flatness within 0.5 mm/m.
capabilitiesDescription: Our facility combines 6 kW fiber laser cutting systems (4 m × 2 m bed) with 60,000 psi abrasive waterjet systems (6 m × 3 m bed), enabling us to cut titanium profiles from prototype quantities to high-volume production across all standard and custom titanium alloys.

downstreamProcesses.name: Deburring & Edge Finishing
downstreamProcesses.description: Mechanical deburring (wheel brush, drag finishing) or chemical deburring for laser-cut edges to remove dross and achieve uniform edge radius.

downstreamProcesses.name: Pickling & Passivation
downstreamProcesses.description: Nitric-hydrofluoric acid bath (ASTM B600) removes light oxidation from laser-cut edges and restores uniform corrosion-resistant passive layer.

downstreamProcesses.name: CNC Edge Milling & Drilling
downstreamProcesses.description: 4/5-axis CNC machining of mounting bolt holes, flange faces, and precision edge profiles on cut blanks.

downstreamProcesses.name: TIG Welding & Assembly
downstreamProcesses.description: Automatic orbital TIG welding of profile-joined assemblies with ERTi-2 or ERTi-5 filler wire; weld map documentation included.

downstreamProcesses.name: Dimensional Inspection (CMM)
downstreamProcesses.description: Full 3D CMM inspection of profile geometry, hole positions, and edge contour compliance within ±0.02 mm.

downstreamProcesses.name: Cleanroom Packaging
downstreamProcesses.description: Class 10 / Class 100 cleanroom packaging with VCI anti-corrosion lining for sensitive aerospace and medical applications.
